Soil was collected 1/15/19 in the morning at 8:38am while snowing. I went to Sugarhouse Park in Salt Lake City, UT. The pond was fenced off as they had discovered a strain of Avian botulism there and were digging it up. I went to the back side of the lake and dug about 3-5 inches down in the dirt under a pine tree. The dirt was soft and somewhat sandy/rocky but it was all that was not frozen. It was 24 degrees F and latitude was 40 degrees 43' 26" N while longitude of site was 111 degrees 51' 2" W. This is 4410 feet elevation, and I dug on the East side of the pine tree.

Soil was collected from the organic surroundings beneath a plum tree, in the back yard of a home, located in Murray, UT.  Sample collection was approx. 2-3 feet from the base of a plum tree. A hole was dug at a depth of 25 cm on January 13th 2019 around 1940-1945 in the evening, when the outside temperature was -2 Celsius. The area the sample was collected is note sprayed with any pesticides (organic) and has little to no foot traffic.

The area the sample was collected is note sprayed with any pesticides (organic) and has little to no foot traffic.

The sampling area is located in the CSUS Arboretum. The location is about 2.4 m from a moderately used walkway, and about 0.5 m from a fallen Kentucky Coffee Tree (Gymnocladus dioicus) and about 2 m from a live Cestrum aurantiacum, but under its canopy. The location was covered with foliage and plant debris (mostly fallen pine leaves). No green vegetation was observed at the location, but grass and moss were growing about 15 cm away. The sample was collected from a depth of 5 cm below the surface. The weather conditions were overcast, with slight rainfall about 2 hours prior to sampling. This rainfall rendered the soil wet.

This area is filled with tree's with a gutter passing through. This area is in between dorm residencies ,and has a concrete pavement on each side which makes this area somewhat small but spacious. There were not many plants in plain view, but more so a dirt ground with skinny trees all around. The soil seemed to very hard on the surface, but as I dug I noticed it feeling like sand. It was soft once it was broken down. It also had a dry, powdery feeling as I noticed the wind blowing the tiny particles of dirt on my clothing. I cannot imagine many people coming through this area of tree's because the space is very limited . There is also no pavement or specific place for people to hang around . The weather was beautiful when collecting the soil with sunny skies and soft winds.

Soil sample came from a plant bed in between the concrete lab and Riverside hall. There was a sprinkler to the left of the sample. There was also a ground cover bush covering the sample site. The soil was moist to the touch and cold. There was shade when we collected the soil and tall buildings around the sample site, so there probably isn't much sun throughout the day. People walk through the area regularly but no one walks directly on site of the soil sample. Human impact would only come from people fixing the sprinkler directly to left or landscapers trimming the bush above the soil. There is a compost bin, trash bin, and recycle bin within 5 feet of the soil sample. There is also a bench to the left of the soil sample so people would potentially sit near it as well. Within the same plant bed there was a tree in the middle.

Soil sample came from a plant bed in between the concrete lab and Riverside hall. There was a sprinkler to the left of the sample. There was also a ground cover bush covering the sample site. The soil was moist to the touch and cold. There was shade when we collected the soil and tall buildings around the sample site, so there probably isn't much sun throughout the day. People walk through the area regularly but no one walks directly on site of the soil sample. Human impact would only come from people fixing the sprinkler directly to left or landscapers trimming the bush above the soil. There is a compost bin, trash bin, and recycle bin within 5 feet of the soil sample. There is also a bench to the left of the soil sample so people would potentially sit near it as well. Within the same plant bed there was a tree in the middle.
